title: Claws Out: Securing and Building with OpenClaw - Nick Taylor, Pomerium
talk_summary: Nick Taylor describes contributing a 'trusted proxy auth mode' to OpenClaw so an identity-aware proxy (Pomerium) can gate the control plane, removing per-connection tokens and device pairing. The rest is a live demo of building an MCP app by chatting to an agent in Discord, plus anecdotes about PR rebasing and an agent opening a PR prematurely.

takeaways.technique: Trusted-proxy auth for agent control planes
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of per-connection tokens and device pairing, the gateway trusts a specific proxy IP and reads identity from a header (JWT), with policy enforced upstream by the identity-aware proxy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's trusted proxies. And this is essentially the proxy that is gating access to the control plane

takeaways.technique: MCP server with UI for agent-built tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Registers an MCP server (echo + search tools) with an attached UI so tool calls render interactive widgets; the agent edits the workspace files and hot-reloads them live.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's got a echo tool and it's got a search speakers tool

takeaways.what_they_do: Agent given full GitHub CLI access opened a PR before the human finished reviewing; they recovered by converting it back to draft.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I gave it full access. So, it put up a PR right away even before I was like done reviewing things

takeaways.technique: Test on clean state, not just your own env
takeaways.what_they_do: The contributor tested locally where a device was already paired, so a bug only surfaced for a fresh user and was caught by a community reporter.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I basically was testing this on my local environment and I already had something paired

takeaways.what_they_do: A PR went stale in two weeks as the repo grew from ~1,500 to ~16,000 issues, forcing heavy rebasing before merge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it went from like 1500 to like almost 16,000
